In Phase 5 of the CSI Pacific ACL Rehabilitation Protocol, the off-field components become secondary to on-field training, however the importance of these components does not diminish at all. The goal of this section is to help everyone involved with the rehab to navigate the complexities of returning to sport and to performance, while continuing to care for the knee with a high degree of attention to detail. Phase 5 will be highly individualized based on the sport that the athlete competes in, and while it is not possible to cover specific details for all sports, there remain principles and fundamentals which inform best practice during this critical phase. We hope that the resources provided in this chapter will make it easier to navigate these complexities by providing a highly organized and detailed road-map for continuing a successful rehab which supports improvements in on-field performance.

::: {.callout-important title="Most Important Goals — Phase 3"}
- Performance on all dynamic tasks exceeds 95% of pre-injury or opposite leg performance

```{r}
tbl_phase5 <- criteria_phase5_abr %>%
  transmute(
```

```{r}

goals_progress_bar <- function(
    met, total,
    label = "Goals met",
    width = "100%",
    accent = "#D71920",   # table accent (red)
    border = "#A7A9AC",   # table border grey
    track_bg = "#FCFCFC", # header/stripe light bg
    fill_from = "#2E7D32",# green gradient start
    fill_to   = "#4CAF50" # green gradient end
) {
  pct <- if (total > 0) round(100 * met / total) else 0
  
  tagList(
    tags$style(HTML(sprintf("
      .ak-pb-wrap   { margin-top:12px; font-family:'Open Sans',system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,Roboto,Arial,sans-serif; }
      .ak-pb-meta   { display:flex; justify-content:space-between; font-size:0.95rem; margin-bottom:6px; color:#222; }
      .ak-pb-meta strong{ color:%s; font-weight:700; } /* accent like table title */
      .ak-pb       { background:%s; border:1px solid %s; border-radius:10px; height:14px; overflow:hidden; }
      .ak-pb__fill { height:100%%; background:linear-gradient(90deg,%s,%s); transition:width .3s ease; }
    ", accent, track_bg, border, fill_from, fill_to))),
    div(class = "ak-pb-wrap",
        div(class = "ak-pb-meta",
            tags$strong(sprintf("%s: %d/%d", label, met, total)),
            span(sprintf("%d%%", pct))
        ),
        div(
          class = "ak-pb",
          role = "progressbar",
          `aria-valuemin` = "0",
          `aria-valuemax` = "100",
          `aria-valuenow` = pct,
          style = sprintf("width:%s;", width),
          div(class = "ak-pb__fill", style = sprintf("width:%d%%;", pct))
        )
    )
  )
}

total_n_all <- nrow(criteria_phase5_abr)

goals_progress_bar(met_n_all, total_n_all)
```

## What does the research say? {#preop-outcomes}

> "Completion of the rehabilitation protocol and clearance to return to sport is not the same as return to competition. Before clearance for return to unrestricted competition, there should be a transition phase from sports participation to sports performance with progressive and controlled exposure to athlete’s sport" @ardern2016

It is important that training continues, and criteria are consistently re-evaluated as the athlete returns to regular training and competition.

Neuromuscular training returns to it's place as being secondary to sport training. The athlete's schedule is no longer built around what is optimal physiologically, rather it must be adapted to fit with the daily and weekly training schedules of the sport. For example, workouts may now occur following practices and games, when fatigue may play a factor in force production @buckthorpe2014 or movement quality @vanmelick2019.

Continued testing of Phase 5 criteria are important for ensuring that the athlete does not compromise the physical, mental and emotional gains made throughout the rehab.

Additional measures of sporting performance after RTS should be recorded and monitored to ascertain if the athlete has RTPerf (eg, number of matches played, goals scored, assists, number of pitches, wickets, etc, depending on the sport and performance requirements). @buckthorpe2019b

### Warm Up

Is there research or does this go in additional resources?

The warm-up becomes extremely crucial for this athlete for the rest of their career in order to optimally prepare for training/competition, and also as a n opportunity to target specific neuromuscular needs on a constant basis, and while feeling fresh before undergoing the demands of the sport.

## Testing

Each card below contains a detailed description of the tests to be conducted during this phase of rehab.

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}


tests <- criteria_phase5 |>
  dplyr::select(outcome_measure, display_description, additional_information, operator_pretty, goal_pretty, repetitions, calculation, image_path) %>%
  mutate(op_goal = paste(operator_pretty, goal_pretty)) %>%
    filter(!outcome_measure %in% c(
      "CMJ Lengthening Asymmetry",
      "CMJ Shortening Asymmetry"
  ))

# Helper: print a label/value line only if value is non-missing & non-empty
emit_field <- function(label, value) {
  if (length(value) == 0 || all(is.na(value))) return(invisible())
  val <- value[[1]]
  if (is.na(val)) return(invisible())
  val_chr <- trimws(as.character(val))
  if (!nzchar(val_chr)) return(invisible())
  cat("**", label, ":** ", val_chr, "\n\n", sep = "")
}

for (i in seq_len(nrow(tests))) {

  cat('::: {.card .ak-card .has-stripe .accent-primary}\n')

  # ---- TITLE ----
  cat('### ', tests$outcome_measure[i], '\n\n', sep = '')

  # ---- FULL-WIDTH TEXT ----
  if (!is.na(tests$display_description[i]) &&
      nzchar(trimws(tests$display_description[i]))) {
    cat(tests$display_description[i], '\n\n')
  }

  cat("*", tests$additional_information[i], '\n\n')

# ---- BOTTOM ROW (FLEX) ----
cat('<div style="display:flex; gap:1.5rem; align-items:center;">\n')

# LEFT: CRITERIA BLOCK (slightly narrower)
cat('<div style="flex:0 0 35%;">\n')
emit_field("Criteria", tests$op_goal[i])
emit_field("Repetitions", tests$repetitions[i])
emit_field("Calculation", tests$calculation[i])
cat('</div>\n')

# RIGHT: IMAGE (wider + centered)
cat('<div style="flex:0 0 65%; text-align:center;">\n')
if (!is.na(tests$image_path[i]) && nzchar(trimws(tests$image_path[i]))) {
  cat('<img src="', tests$image_path[i],
      '" style="max-width:80%; max-height:220px; object-fit:contain; display:inline-block;" />\n',
      sep = '')
}
cat('</div>\n')

cat('</div>\n')  # end flex row

  cat(':::\n\n')  # end card
}

```
